(There's a bug report and some back and forth below,
but first a general note how to report bugs.)

I can see how that page full of controls for the
issue tracker could be intimidating if you're not
used to issue trackers. All you really need to do
is to click on "new issue" and proceed. I'll add some
instructions to the web page and also indicate that
users can just mail us bug reports at:

bu...@mc-stan.org.

Using the issue tracker helps us keep track of them, but
we can enter them ourselves if we can't fix them right
away.

Agustï¿½n: Did you have a previous version of RStan installed?
Did you manage to install the developer tools and get Rcpp
working? There's a diagnostic in the install instructions to
let you check if Rcpp is working (and hence the whole C++ tool
chain is properly installed).

If you haven't, could you please run the simple
Rcpp example in the install instructions? (You can just
mail us back at bu...@mc-stan.org or just mail me directly
if you're not on our user's mailing list.)

Is anyone else having problems installing RStan?

I don't think anything changed on our side, but
we're getting a slew of bug reports for odd behavior.

- Bob
